CITY OF INGLEWOOD

City Council Chambers – Ninth Floor (Planning Commission & Staff)
1 West Manchester Boulevard

  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

Until further notice, meetings of the Inglewood Planning Commission will
be conducted pursuant to California Government Code section 54953(e),
which allows the City to use teleconferencing for members of the public to
access a meeting and to address the legislative body via a call-in option.

CALL-IN OPTION
1.  Members of the public who wish to attend the Planning Commission
Meeting of November 2, 2022 and address the Planning Commission must use
the call-in option noted below:
Instructions: Dial one of the Phone Numbers below and when prompted,
enter the Access Code:
  Phone Number: 888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694
  Access Code: 4693811#
In the event of a disruption which prevents the City from broadcasting the
meeting to the public using the call-in option, or in the event of a
disruption within the City’s control which prevents the public from
offering public comments using the call-in option, the Planning Commission
shall take no further action on items appearing on the meeting agenda
until public access to the meeting via the call-in option is restored.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City also provides alternative methods for members of the public to
submit comments and/or to observe a public meeting. The following
alternative methods are provided to the public as a matter of convenience
only and the disruption in service to any alternative method does not
preclude the Planning Commission from taking further action on an agenda
item.  In the event of a disruption to any alternative method below
members of the public should use the call-in option above.
2. Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may
choose to submit comments for consideration by the Planning Commission by
sending  them  to  Mindy  Wilcox,  AICP,  Planning  Manager  at
mwilcox@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the
Planning Commission prior to consideration of the agenda, comments must be
received prior to 12:00 P.M. on the day of the meeting. Correspondence
should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after
12:00 P.M. and prior to the close of the public hearing will be made part
of the official public record of the meeting.
3. Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please
check  with your cable provider for details
  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video at
  https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

Accessibility: If you will require special accommodations due to a
disability, please contact the Planning Division Office at (310) 412-5230,
One Manchester Boulevard, 4th Floor, Inglewood, California 90301.  All
requests for accommodations must be received 48 hours prior to the day of
the hearing.
Español: "Si no entiende esta noticia o si necesita más información, favor
de llamar a este número (310) 412-5230."

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 2, 2022

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, November 2, 2022, in the City
Council Chambers, on the ninth floor, of City Hall. Following the
Pledge of Allegiance by Commissioner Shaw-Williams, the meeting
was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present: Chairman Larry Springs
  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams
Excused
Absence: Commissioner Aidé Trejo
  Commissioner David Rice

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Planner
  Christine Rivera, Assistant Planner
  Sean May, Planning Technician
  Michael Pan, Assistant City Attorney
  Cynthia Robinson, Secretary
  Via Community Phone Call Coverage:
  AT&T Conference Call Operator Rep.

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Ms. Mindy Wilcox stated that staff received communication that
Commissioner Trejo and Rice will not be in attendance tonight. Ms.
Wilcox also stated that there is a clarification on Item 7A on the
agenda, the correct design review number is Design Review 2022-
010. She also stated that staff received notice that the South Bay
Cities Council of Government will be hosting a housing webinar
series in January and information will be provided in the coming
weeks or month.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None (Confirmed by AT&T Operator).

(5) MINUTES APPROVAL:
Chairman Springs called for a motion to approve October 5, 2022
minutes.

Motion to Approve October 5, 2022 Minutes by Commissioner Shaw-
Williams and seconded by Commissioner Patrick.

The motion passed with the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Shaw-Williams, and Chairman
  Springs.

(6) PUBLIC HEARING:

6A. GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT NO. 2022-002 (GPA-2022-008).
A public hearing to consider General Plan Amendment 2022-002 (GPA-
2022-002) to update the Safety Element of the Inglewood General
Plan.
  This item is postponed to December 7, 2022 meeting.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
November 2, 2022

(7) NON-PUBLIC HEARING:

7A. DESIGN REVIEW 2022-010 (DR-2022-010).
Design Review 2022-010 (DR-2022-010) to allow exterior
alterations to an existing one-story commercial building, on an
H-C (Historic Core) zoned property at 213 South La Brea Avenue.

Mr. Angel Leon-Martell,  Assistant  Planner,  made  the  staff
presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick asked staff –
  Will the alley entrance remain the entrance for all of the
  other occupants of the building?
  How many parking spaces are there going to be.
  - Mr. Leon-Martell responded to Commissioner Patrick’s
  questions.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked staff –
  What are the operating hours?
  - Mr. Leon-Martell responded to Commissioner Patrick’s
  questions.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for the Planning Commission to
address the applicant.
Chairman Springs asked the applicant to give their name and talk
about their project.

Brion Moran, the architect for the project, addressed the Planning
Commission.

Chairman Springs asked the Commissioners if they had any questions
for the applicant.

Commissioner Patrick asked the applicant –
 Will this Urgent Care Center be tied to a Hospital?
  - Mr. Moran responded to Commissioner Patrick’s question.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked the applicant –
 How many physicians will be at this location?
  - Mr. Moran responded to Commissioner Shaw-Williams’s question.

Chairman Springs closed the non-public hearing and called for a
motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Shaw-Williams made the motion to affirm categorical
exemption EA-CE-2022-107 and adopt a resolution approving DR-2022-
010 subject to 9 conditions, and/or add conditions as deemed
appropriate and was seconded by Commissioner Patrick that

  010 TO APPROVE EXTERIOR ALTERATIONS TO AN
  EXISTING ONE-STORY COMMERCIAL BUILDING, ON
  AN H-C (HISTORIC CORE) ZONED PROPERTY.

Be approved.

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Shaw-Williams, and
  Chairman Springs.

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeal process.

(8) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None, (Confirmed by AT&T Operator).

Chairman Springs closed the hearings to the public and asked for
the Planning Commission Initiatives.

(9) COMMISSION INITIATIVES:
Commissioner Patrick -
 Would like to encourage everyone to go out and vote for the
  candidate of your choice.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams –
 Agreed with Commissioner Patrick to get out and vote and have a
  happy Thanksgiving.

Chairman Springs –
 Agreed with Commissioner Patrick as well and stated that this
  election is extremely important. He stated that the city is
  growing.

(10) ADJOURNMENT:
Chairman Springs adjourned tonight’s meeting at 7:20pm.
